assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing item operations, coupon logic, total calculation, and checkout.
assertions.evidence: Five @TableTest methods: addsItemsFromTheCatalogue, removesItemsFromTheCart, appliesCouponsToTheCart, checksOutTheCart, calculatesTheCartTotal

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Add has 6 rows (new, stack, unknown, zero, negative); Remove has 4 rows; Apply has 7 rows; Checkout has 7 rows; Total has 10 rows. Each focuses on its operation.

assertions.text: Item operations (add/remove), coupon application (validity and replacement), cart total calculation (coupon type effects on price), and checkout (stock verification) are in separate @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: appliesCouponsToTheCart tests validity/replacement only (no price calculation); calculatesTheCartTotal tests price effects (no validity checks); checksOutTheCart tests stock only

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable — no row depends on a prior row's result. The table expresses rules, not a sequential test script. Each row specifies its own preconditions.
assertions.evidence: Each row in all tables specifies complete preconditions (e.g., 'Cart Before', 'Catalogue', 'Stock') with no implicit dependencies on prior rows

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses before/after columns (e.g. 'Active coupon' / 'Active coupon after?') to specify the state change when entering, replacing, or entering invalid coupon codes.
assertions.evidence: appliesCouponsToTheCart uses 'Active Coupon Before' and 'Active Coupon After?' columns showing state transitions (e.g., SAVE10 → FIVEOFF, SAVE10 → SAVE10 on expired)

assertions.text: Coupon application table tests validity and replacement (valid code, expired code, nonexistent code, replacing active coupon) — not coupon type effects on price. Coupon type effects belong in the cart total table.
assertions.evidence: appliesCouponsToTheCart tests PERCENT/FIXED/PRODUCT validity and replacement; calculatesTheCartTotal tests price effects (PERCENT 20 → 16.00, FIXED 5.00 → 15.00)

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Message?', 'Total?', 'Active coupon after?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Cart After?, Success?, Message?, Cart After?, Success?, Message?, Active Coupon After?, Success?, Message?, Success?, Message Mentions?, Total?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Add to empty cart', 'Replace active coupon with expired') — not outcomes ('Error', 'Success').
assertions.evidence: Scenarios like 'Add new item to empty cart', 'Expired coupon does not replace the active coupon', 'Insufficient stock by one unit' describe conditions, not outcomes

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Product', 'Quantity', 'Message?', 'Cart total?') — not code identifiers like 'productId', 'result'.
assertions.evidence: Column 'Product Id' uses code-ism 'Id' where cell values are product names (Widget); should be 'Product'. Also 'Cart Items' vs 'Cart Before' inconsistency.

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 5 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 5 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method applies one uniform assertion pattern to every row — not different assertions per scenario. Several unconditional assertions checking distinct observable outputs of one result (e.g. success, message, resulting cart) count as one uniform pattern; the anti-pattern is branching on the row (if/switch/ternary/try-catch) to choose what is asserted.
assertions.evidence: 5 method(s) apply one uniform assertion pattern to all rows

assertions.text: Product prices and coupon rules (type, amount, expiry status) are visible in the table via columns, @Description, or explicit setup — not silently hardcoded. The reader can trace how inputs lead to outputs.
assertions.evidence: Catalogue column shows prices [Widget: 10.00]; Coupon In Store shows definitions (PERCENT 10, FIXED 5.00, PRODUCT Widget 3.00, EXPIRED); @Description explains assumptions

assertions.text: TypeConverter methods are used to convert map/string table values into domain objects (e.g. Map → Cart, Map → InventoryService, map → Coupon). Test method bodies contain only arrange-act-assert — no object construction from raw table values.
assertions.evidence: @TypeConverter methods: parseCatalogue, parseCart, parseInventory, parseCoupon. Method bodies call CartService directly without constructing objects from raw values.

assertions.text: Coupon data is expressed in a single column with a @TypeConverter — not spread across separate sparse columns for coupon type, value, and target product.
assertions.evidence: The `appliesCouponsToTheCart` table has a single 'Coupon In Store' column with values like 'PERCENT 10', 'FIXED 5.00', 'PRODUCT Widget 3.00', 'EXPIRED', or blank. The `parseCoupon` @TypeConverter converts these strings into Coupon objects.

assertions.text: Columns representing maps use standard TableTest map syntax — [k: v, k2: v2] for entries and [:] for empty map — not a custom bracket notation.
assertions.evidence: All map columns use standard syntax: 'Catalogue' shows '[Widget: 9.99]', '[Widget: 9.99, Gadget: 4.50]'; 'Cart Before/After' shows '[:]', '[Widget: 2]', '[Widget: 1, Gadget: 3]'; 'Stock' shows '[Widget: 5]', '[:]'. @TypeConverters parse these into domain objects.

assertions.text: @Description annotations do not merely repeat information that the scenario names already convey.
assertions.evidence: The `addsItemsFromTheCatalogue` @Description states 'Adding a product already in the cart increases its quantity rather than replacing it (assumption — the rules don't state this explicitly)' and 'Quantity must be a positive integer', which are design decisions not evident from scenario names alone. The `appliesCouponsToTheCart` @Description explains the 'Coupon In Store' encoding (definition, EXPIRED, or blank), which is necessary context for reading the table.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: In `addsItemsFromTheCatalogue`, the 'Cart After?' column varies: '[Widget: 2]', '[Widget: 1, Gadget: 3]', '[Widget: 3]', '[:]', '[:]', '[Widget: 1]' — not all identical. In `calculatesTheCartTotal`, 'Total?' varies: '30.00', '40.00', '16.00', '15.00', '0.00', '0.00', '20.00', '5.00', '0.00', '0.00'. No row is a verbatim copy of an input column.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: The 'Quantity must be positive' rule is stated in the @Description and demonstrated by rows with 0 and -2. The 'floor at zero' rule is shown by the 'Fixed coupon exceeds the subtotal, floored' row (25.00 discount on 20.00 subtotal → 0.00) and 'Empty cart, any coupon' row. The 'product coupon ignored when product absent' rule is explicit in the scenario name and row values.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or the method name it falls back to) states what the code under test does, not an external fact it depends on.
assertions.evidence: Method names are 'addsItemsFromTheCatalogue', 'removesItemsFromTheCart', 'appliesCouponsToTheCart', 'checksOutTheCart', 'calculatesTheCartTotal' — all describe CartService actions. Removing 'CartService' from 'CartService adds items' leaves 'adds items', which is what the system does, not an external fact.
